description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
We successfully trained 19 Cca staff in this programme and all participants were present during the training period.
From the evaluation we can tell the training made good impact on the participants. We know 4 participants have started their own poultry farm. through the entrepreneur skills which we included in our training they were able to start this business.
Through Whatsapp we still get updates from our interpreter about progress made in poultry farming. This tells us that participants are still active in spreading knowledge. However, due to the difficulties in the internet connection it is almost impossible to get reports or successtories in return.
​
George Dramani starting with broilers:
Be sure, we were satisfied with the depth and quality of the training received. The only remaining challenge for most trainees is the lack of start-up funds for professional breeding. By the end of 2024 I plan to achieve savings of 10,000 euros to start with 1000 broiler hens; not to mention the others who are seriously considering getting into the commercial and professional dimension.
​
From a mail from Brigitte:
Oui, nous sommes en train de nous battre une implantation prochaine des poules pondeuses et à chair.
Les difficultés, il y en aura toujours, mais nous ne pouvons pas nous décourager.
Beaucoup de courage pour vous aussi
Brigitte

comment.narrative: 21-06-2023: Ceca 2020 is the requesting organisation and 19 people were trained in our programme. Ceca 2020 is the organisation benefitting from the training programme. In the group of trainees were 2 staff members of the Shalom University, this is the 2nd organisation benefitting from this programme. The Ceca participants are from 5 different regions which means the knowledge will not be available in only 1 region but it is spread over the regions in the eastern part of DR Cong.

title.narrative: B.I.6. Number of stimulating measures/extra facilities aimed at preparation, supervision and aftercare of female candidates

comment.narrative: 21-06-2023: In the application form we stated already that in case of equal qualification preference will be given to women in the programme. In the invitation for the selection procedure we stated that ladies will be given preference in case of equal level. During the programme we give equal attention to every participant. We also made use of female local trainers for specific parts of the training programme (see picture) We know from 4 participants they have started poultry farming out of which there are 2 ladies. We also heard that 1 lady participant has trained a group of lady farmers. We do not recieve reports stating how many farmers actually have been trained.
